claims.text: A 7-metal high-entropy spinel oxide has greater configurational disorder than a 4-metal medium-entropy spinel oxide.
Increasing configurational disorder by moving from a 4-metal to a 7-metal spinel improves CO oxidation activity.
Increasing configurational disorder by moving from a 4-metal to a 7-metal spinel improves long-term catalytic durability.
The 7-metal high-entropy spinel will reduce platinum-group-metal consumption relative to a 4-metal catalyst.
Conventional 4-metal spinel catalysts used in automotive exhaust require significant PGM content to achieve acceptable CO oxidation performance.
Additional transition metals can be incorporated homogeneously into a spinel lattice.
The reported catalytic improvement occurs under dry, lean conditions with excess oxygen.
Dry, lean conditions are representative of typical automotive exhaust streams.
Increasing configurational disorder decreases the spinel lattice parameter.
Increasing configurational disorder increases oxygen-vacancy concentration.
The structural changes caused by increased disorder create a more diverse and uniformly distributed array of active sites.
Random cation distributions and additional oxygen vacancies improve the redox flexibility of the spinel oxide.
Random cation distributions and additional oxygen vacancies increase active-site density.
The proposed redox and active-site changes lower the activation temperature for CO oxidation.
The proposed structural mechanism mitigates deactivation pathways and thereby enhances long-term stability.
The 7-metal HESO has a CO-oxidation T10 of 168 °C, approximately 63% lower than the 454 °C T10 of the 4-metal MESO.
The 7-metal HESO should have a higher initial CO conversion rate than the 4-metal baseline.
Over 14 hours, the 7-metal HESO loses 4.7% activity compared with a 12.2% loss for the 4-metal MESO.
The benefits under sulfur- and water-containing feeds remain unvalidated and may be less pronounced.
pXRD and HAADF-STEM can be used to quantify oxygen-vacancy concentration in these catalysts.
